== History ==
[[File:Shirahige-jinja Kawashima ac (2).jpg|thumb|Main hall built atop high stone walls]]

The date of foundation is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was established in the 10th year of the {{ill|Yang Water Rat|af|Waterrot (astrologie)|cdo|Ìng-cṳ̄ (găng-ciĕ)|de|Wasser-Ratte|fr|Rat d'eau (astrologie)|hak|Ngìm-chṳ́|ja|壬子|ko|임자|vi|Nhâm Tý|za|Nyaemzceij|zh|壬子|zh_min_nan|Jîm-chú|zh_yue|壬子|qid=Q904972}} era of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ar|الإمبراطور نينتوكو|arz|الامبراطور نينتوكو|azb|نینتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট নিন্তকু|br|Impalaer Nintoku|ca|Emperador Nintoku|cs|Nintoku|de|Nintoku|es|Nintoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور نینتوکو|fi|Nintoku|fr|Nintoku|hr|Nintoku|hu|Nintoku japán császár|id|Kaisar Nintoku|it|Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|ka|ნინტოკუ|ko|닌토쿠 천황|lt|Imperatorius Nintoku|ms|Maharaja Nintoku|nds|Nintoku|nl|Nintoku|pl|Nintoku|pt|Nintoku|ru|Император Нинтоку|sh|Car Nintoku|simple|Emperor Nintoku|sl|Cesar Nintoku|sv|Nintoku|th|จักรพรรดินินโตกุ|tl|Emperador Nintoku|tr|Nintoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Нінтоку|uz|Imperator Nintoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Nintoku|yo|Emperor Nintoku|zh|仁德天皇|zh_min_nan|Nintoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|仁德天皇|qid=Q313119}} following an imperial decree<ref>If taken as the 10th year of Emperor Nintoku’s reign, this would correspond to 322.</ref>, and a shrine building was constructed in the 4th year of the {{ill|Yin Wood Rabbit|af|Houtkonyn (astrologie)|cdo|Ĭk-māu|de|Holz-Hase|hak|Yet-mâu|ja|乙卯|ko|을묘|vi|Ất Mão|za|Ietmaux|zh|乙卯|zh_min_nan|It-báu|zh_yue|乙卯|qid=Q904791}} era of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|ar|الإمبراطور إنغيو|arz|الامبراطور انجيو|azb|اینقیو (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Ingjó|de|Ingyō|es|Ingyō Tennō|fa|امپراتور اینگیو|fr|Ingyō|hr|Ingyō|id|Kaisar Ingyō|it|Ingyō|ja|允恭天皇|ka|ინგიო|ko|인교 천황|nl|Ingyo|pl|Ingyō|pt|Ingyo|ru|Император Ингё|sh|Car Ingyō|simple|Emperor Ingyō|sl|Cesar Thian-hông|zh_yue|允恭天皇|qid=Q349258}} following another imperial decree<ref>If taken as the 4th year of Emperor Ingyō’s reign, this would correspond to 415.</ref><ref name="由緒">Explanatory signboard “History of Shirahige Shrine.”</ref>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}.

In the 2nd year of {{ill|Reiki (era)|de|Reiki (Ära)|es|Reiki (era)|fa|ریکی (دوره)|fr|Ère Reiki|ia|Reiki (era)|id|Reiki (era)|ja|霊亀|ko|레이키|ru|Рэйки (нэнго)|simple|Reiki (era)|sr|Реики (ера)|th|เรกิ|tr|Reiki (dönem)|uk|Рейкі (ера)|zh|靈龜|zh_yue|靈龜|qid=Q1373115}} (717), Hachiman Shrine was established as a subordinate shrine within the precincts<ref name="八幡神社">From the inscription on the monument marking the former site of Hachiman Shrine within the grounds of the Inaba District Gymnasium, Kakamigahara City.</ref>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 14 (1586), flooding of the {{ill|Kiso River|arz|نهر كيسو|bg|Кисо (река)|ceb|Kiso-gawa|cs|Kiso (řeka)|de|Kiso (Fluss)|es|Río Kiso|eu|Kiso ibaia|fa|رود کیسو|fr|Kiso-gawa|he|קיסו (נהר)|it|Kiso|ja|木曽川|ko|기소강|my|ခိဆိုမြစ်|pl|Kiso|ru|Кисо (река)|tr|Kiso Nehri|uk|Кісо (річка)|zh|木曾川|qid=Q779607}} washed away the shrine buildings. As a result of this flood, a new course of the Kiso River became the boundary between {{ill|Owari Province|ar|أواري|ca|Província d'Owari|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆوواری|cs|Provincie Owari|de|Provinz Owari|es|Provincia de Owari|eu|Owari probintzia|fa|ولایت اوواری|fi|Owarin provinssi|fr|Province d'Owari|gl|Provincia de Owari|hak|Owari-koet|id|Provinsi Owari|it|Owari (provincia)|ja|尾張国|ko|오와리국|lt|Ovario žemė|nl|Owari (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Owari|pt|Província de Owari|ru|Овари (провинция)|simple|Owari Province|sk|Owari (provincia)|sr|Провинција Овари|tr|Owari (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Оварі|vi|Tỉnh Owari|wuu|尾张国|zh|尾張國|zh_min_nan|Owari-kok|zh_yue|尾張國|qid=Q514506}} and {{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}}, and this area changed from Haguri District, Owari Province, to {{ill|Haguri district|ja|羽栗郡|zh|羽栗郡|qid=Q11610214}}, Mino Province. The subordinate Hachiman Shrine was relocated to Majima in Haguri District (present-day {{ill|Kakamigahara|ar|كاكاميغهارا (غيفو)|arz|كاكاميجاهارا, جيفو|azb|کاکامیقاهارا، قیفو|ca|Kakamigahara|ce|Какамигахара|ceb|Kakamigahara (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Kakamigahara|de|Kakamigahara|eo|Kakamigahara|es|Kakamigahara (Gifu)|fa|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|fi|Kakamigahara|fr|Kakamigahara|gl|Kakamigahara|it|Kakamigahara|ja|各務原市|ko|가카미가하라시|mg|Kakamigahara|mr|काकामिगहारा|mzn|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|nl|Kakamigahara|no|Kakamigahara|pl|Kakamigahara|pt|Kakamigahara|ro|Kakamigahara|ru|Какамигахара|sh|Kakamigahara|sr|Какамигахара|su|Kakamigahara, Gifu|sv|Kakamigahara|tg|Какамигаҳара|tl|Kakamigahara, Gifu|tr|Kakamigahara|tt|Какамигахара|uk|Какаміґахара|ur|کاکامیگاہارا، گیفو|vi|Kakamigahara, Gifu|war|Kakamigahara, Gifu|zh|各务原市|zh_classical|各務原市|zh_min_nan|Kakamigahara-chhī|zh_yue|各務原|qid=Q641491}} Kamiochi-chō, at the site of the {{ill|Kakamigahara City Inaba District Gymnasium|ja|各務原市稲羽地区体育館|qid=Q109603254}})<ref name="八幡神社"/>. Thereafter, it was moved to its present location in Kasada, Haguri District, by {{ill|Tsubouchi Toshisada|ja|坪内利定|qid=Q11425729}}, a {{ill|Shinkanō Jin'ya|ja|新加納陣屋|qid=Q11501438}} of high rank stationed at {{ill|Shinkanō Jin'ya|ja|新加納陣屋|qid=Q11501438}} (former lord of {{ill|Matsukura Castle|ja|松倉城 (尾張国)|ko|마쓰쿠라성 (오와리국)|qid=Q11239240|lt=Matsukura Castle}})<ref name="由緒"/>{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}. It was renamed Shirahige Myōjin and later changed to Shirahige Shrine.

During the Meiji period, it became a village shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}. After World War II, it was designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|ja|金幣社|qid=Q119929592|lt=Shirohei-sha}} by the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines.

In 1999 (Heisei 11), the worship hall, norito hall, main hall, {{ill|banpei|ja|蕃塀|qid=Q124160302}}, and other structures were newly built, and Shinmei Shrine was enshrined together<ref>The former location was 1266 Koyabajima, Kasada-chō. It is now within {{ill|Water Eco Park|ja|河川環境楽園|qid=Q11553849}}.</ref>.

== Subordinate shrines ==
Originally, there were two subordinate shrines: Kaijin Shrine and Akiba Shrine{{sfn|Kawashima Town|1982|p=1174}}. In 1996 (Heisei 8), nearby shrines were absorbed and incorporated as subordinate shrines.
